evals.query: Our Socket.IO 4 app runs as 3 Node.js containers behind nginx on Kubernetes. Since we went from 1 to 3 replicas, browsers log HTTP 400 errors with {"code":1,"message":"Session ID unknown"}, users connected to replica A do not get messages emitted on replica B, and connections drop every 60 seconds or so. We also want missed messages to be restored after a short network loss. Tell me what to change, with code.
expected_behavior: Explains that Session ID unknown means sticky sessions are missing and that they are required while HTTP long-polling is enabled, whatever the adapter

evals.query: Write a Socket.IO 4.8 client and server snippet where the browser sends 'order:create' and must be sure the server stored the order exactly once, even if the connection drops while sending. expected_behavior: Uses the client retries and ackTimeout options (or timeout() with a retry) so the event is sent at least once

Acknowledges duplicates on the server (calls the callback) so the client stops retrying, and does not acknowledge on other errors

evals.query: In our Socket.IO 4 server we store socket.id in the users table at connection time so a background job can later do io.to(user.socketId).emit('notification', data). Some notifications never arrive, especially after users refresh the page or open a second tab. Also our client code does socket.on('connect', () => { socket.on('notification', render); }) and some users see each notification several times. Fix both problems.
expected_behavior: Explains socket.id is regenerated on every reconnection and page refresh, differs per tab and has no queue, so it must not be stored as a user identifier
Joins a room named after the user ID (derived from a session or auth payload validated in a middleware) and emits with io.to(userId).emit
Moves the client listener out of the connect handler to top level, because connect fires on every reconnection
Mentions that the server stores no message, so notifications sent while the user is offline need persistence or replay
